blocks.html: We identify the specific gasket or seal requiring replacement, drain the engine oil where relevant, and remove components obstructing access — including engine covers, intake manifolds, exhaust components, and in some cases subframe, suspension parts, or exhaust pipes.

Once access is achieved, we remove the old gasket or seal using scrapers and appropriate tools. The mating surfaces — both the component and the engine block sealing surfaces — are thoroughly cleaned using metal surface cleaner meeting Jaguar specification. Surface preparation is critical to ensure a proper seal.

We install the new gasket or seal. For some applications, we apply a specific sealant pattern — for example, a 10 mm dot of silicone gasket sealant meeting Jaguar specification applied to the engine block and front cover mating surface. For cylinder head rear cover gaskets, the sealing bead must face the cylinder head surface and no additional sealant is used.

Components are reassembled with bolts torqued to manufacturer specifications in the correct sequence. The engine oil is refilled (where drained), and the engine is run to check for leaks around the repaired area.

sections.heading: Our oil leak and gasket repair process

steps.title: Vehicle arrival & leak tracing
steps.body: We visually inspect the engine bay and use UV dye and UV light to trace the exact source of the leak.

steps.title: Component removal for access
steps.body: We remove engine covers, intake manifolds, exhaust components, or subframe/suspension parts as required.

steps.title: Old gasket removal & surface preparation
steps.body: We remove the old gasket using scrapers, then clean the mating surfaces with metal surface cleaner meeting Jaguar specification.

steps.title: New gasket / seal installation
steps.body: We install the new gasket or seal, applying specific sealant patterns where required, and ensure proper seating.

steps.title: Reassembly with correct torque
steps.body: Components are reassembled with bolts torqued to manufacturer specifications in the correct sequence.

steps.title: Oil refill, engine run & leak check
steps.body: We refill the engine oil, run the engine to operating temperature, and check the repaired area for leaks.

items.q: What does the oil leak repair process involve?
items.a: We identify the specific gasket or seal requiring replacement, drain the engine oil where relevant, and remove components obstructing access. We then remove the old gasket, clean the mating surfaces, install the new gasket or seal, and reassemble components with bolts torqued to manufacturer specifications. The engine is run to check for leaks.

items.q: What gaskets and seals do you replace?
items.a: We replace valve cover gaskets, sump/oil pan gaskets, timing cover gaskets, cylinder head rear cover gaskets, front crank seals, and rear main seals. We also address half-moon seals on AJ133/AJ126 engines.

items.q: How long does the repair take?
items.a: The repair time depends on the specific gasket or seal and the level of access required. Some repairs are relatively straightforward, while others — such as sump gasket replacement — require removing subframe or exhaust components. We provide a clear timeline when we quote the work.

items.q: Do you provide a warranty on the repair?
items.a: Yes. All our repairs come with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty covering parts and labour.
